title: 1451. Who founded the Mauryan Empire?
hint: He established the empire with the guidance of Chanakya.
summary: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE.

title: 1452. Who was the famous adviser of Chandragupta Maurya?
hint: He is also known as Kautilya.
summary: Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, was the chief adviser of Chandragupta Maurya.

title: 1453. What was the capital of the Mauryan Empire?
hint: It was an ancient city located in present-day Bihar.
summary: Pataliputra was the capital of the Mauryan Empire.

title: 1454. Which Greek ruler was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya?
hint: He was a successor of Alexander the Great.
summary: Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus I Nicator and later concluded a treaty with him.

title: 1455. Which Greek ambassador visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
hint: He wrote an account called Indica.
summary: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya's court.

title: 1456. Who succeeded Chandragupta Maurya?
hint: He was the father of Ashoka.
summary: Bindusara succeeded Chandragupta Maurya as the Mauryan emperor.

title: 1457. Who was the most famous ruler of the Mauryan Empire?
hint: He embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War.
summary: Ashoka was the most prominent Mauryan ruler and is renowned for spreading Buddhism and promoting Dhamma.

title: 1458. Which war had a major influence on Ashoka's later policy?
hint: It took place in present-day Odisha.
summary: The Kalinga War deeply affected Ashoka and influenced his later policy of Dhamma and non-violence.

title: 1459. Which ancient text is attributed to Kautilya?
hint: It deals with statecraft, administration and economics.
summary: The Arthashastra is traditionally attributed to Kautilya, also known as Chanakya.

title: 1460. What was the main language used in most of Ashoka's inscriptions?
hint: Many of his inscriptions were written in a Middle Indo-Aryan language.
summary: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were written in Prakrit, generally using the Brahmi script.

title: 1461. Who succeeded Bindusara as the Mauryan emperor?
hint: He is famous for his rock and pillar edicts.
summary: Ashoka succeeded his father Bindusara and became one of the most famous Mauryan rulers.

title: 1462. Which edict of Ashoka describes his remorse after the Kalinga War?
hint: It is one of the Major Rock Edicts.
summary: The 13th Major Rock Edict describes the Kalinga War and Ashoka's remorse over the suffering caused by it.

title: 1463. What name did Ashoka commonly use for his policy of ethical conduct?
hint: It emphasized moral behavior, tolerance and welfare.
summary: Ashoka promoted a policy known as Dhamma, emphasizing ethical conduct, tolerance and social harmony.

title: 1464. Which site is famous for the Lion Capital associated with Ashoka?
hint: It is the place where Buddha delivered his first sermon.
summary: The Lion Capital at Sarnath is a famous Mauryan sculpture and is the basis of India's State Emblem.

title: 1465. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the construction of the original Sanchi Stupa?
hint: He promoted Buddhism after the Kalinga War.
summary: The original Sanchi Stupa is traditionally attributed to Ashoka, while later rulers enlarged and embellished it.

title: 1466. Which script was used in most of Ashoka's inscriptions?
hint: It was an ancient Indian script that later developed into several scripts.
summary: Brahmi was the script used in most of Ashoka's inscriptions, while Kharosthi was used mainly in the northwest.

title: 1467. What was the title used by Ashoka in many of his inscriptions?
hint: It means roughly 'Beloved of the Gods, He Who Looks with Affection'.
summary: Ashoka used the title Devanampiya Piyadasi in many of his inscriptions.

title: 1468. Which caves are associated with the Mauryan period and the Ajivika sect?
hint: They are located in the Barabar hills of Bihar.
summary: The Barabar Caves in Bihar were excavated during the Mauryan period and several were dedicated to the Ajivikas.

title: 1469. Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
hint: He was killed by Pushyamitra Shunga.
summary: Brihadratha was the last Mauryan ruler and was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga around 185 BCE.

title: 1470. Which dynasty succeeded the Mauryan dynasty in Magadha?
hint: Its founder was Pushyamitra.
summary: The Shunga dynasty succeeded the Mauryan dynasty in Magadha after Pushyamitra Shunga overthrew Brihadratha.

title: 1471. Which ancient Greek work provides information about the Mauryan Empire?
hint: It was written by a Greek ambassador who visited Chandragupta Maurya's court.
summary: Indica, written by Megasthenes, provides valuable information about Mauryan India.

title: 1472. Who wrote the Arthashastra?
hint: He was also known as Chanakya.
summary: The Arthashastra is traditionally attributed to Kautilya, also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta.

title: 1473. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the Barabar Cave inscriptions?
hint: He was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya.
summary: Ashoka dedicated several Barabar caves to the Ajivikas, and his inscriptions are found at the site.

title: 1474. Which religious group received cave donations from Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha?
hint: The group was a contemporary ascetic sect.
summary: The Ajivikas received donations of caves during the Mauryan period, particularly at Barabar and Nagarjuni.

title: 1475. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with the spread of Buddhism beyond India?
hint: He sent Buddhist missions to several regions.
summary: Ashoka played a major role in the spread of Buddhism through missions and royal patronage.

title: 1476. What was the main purpose of Ashoka's edicts?
hint: They communicated the ruler's policies and moral principles.
summary: Ashoka's edicts communicated his Dhamma, administrative instructions, moral principles and messages to his subjects.

title: 1477. Which Mauryan ruler made a treaty with Seleucus I Nicator?
hint: He was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty.
summary: Chandragupta Maurya concluded a treaty with Seleucus I Nicator after conflict between their realms.

title: 1478. Which city served as an important provincial center under the Mauryas and later became associated with Ashoka?
hint: It was an important ancient city in western India.
summary: Ujjain was an important Mauryan provincial center, and Ashoka is traditionally associated with having served there as a prince.

title: 1479. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with the Third Buddhist Council?
hint: The council was held at Pataliputra.
summary: The Third Buddhist Council is traditionally said to have been held during Ashoka's reign at Pataliputra.

title: 1480. Which Mauryan ruler is mentioned in Greek sources as Amitrochates?
hint: He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya.
summary: Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, is identified with Amitrochates in Greek accounts.

title: 1481. Which Mauryan ruler is credited with building a large network of roads and promoting public welfare?
hint: He issued numerous inscriptions across his empire.
summary: Ashoka promoted public welfare measures and instructed officials to work for the welfare of people and animals.

title: 1482. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with the spread of Buddhism to Sri Lanka?
hint: His son and daughter are traditionally associated with the Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka.
summary: Ashoka is traditionally associated with the Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka, led by his son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta.

title: 1483. Who was Mahinda in the context of Ashoka's reign?
hint: He is traditionally described as Ashoka's son.
summary: Mahinda is traditionally described in Sri Lankan Buddhist sources as Ashoka's son who led a Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka.

title: 1484. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the famous pillar at Sarnath?
hint: The pillar has four lions standing back to back.
summary: Ashoka commissioned the Sarnath pillar, whose Lion Capital became the basis of India's State Emblem.

title: 1485. What animal appears at the top of the Ashokan Lion Capital at Sarnath?
hint: There are four of them facing different directions.
summary: The Sarnath Lion Capital has four Asiatic lions standing back to back.

title: 1486. Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally said to have embraced Jainism toward the end of his life?
hint: He was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
summary: According to Jain traditions, Chandragupta Maurya became associated with Jainism and spent his final years at Shravanabelagola.

title: 1487. Where is Chandragupta Maurya traditionally believed to have spent his final years?
hint: It is a famous Jain pilgrimage site in Karnataka.
summary: Jain tradition associates Chandragupta Maurya's final years with Shravanabelagola in present-day Karnataka.

title: 1488. Which Mauryan ruler is known from Greek accounts as Amitraghata or Amitrochates?
hint: He was the father of Ashoka.
summary: Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya and father of Ashoka, is associated with the name Amitrochates in Greek accounts.

title: 1489. Which Mauryan ruler appointed officials known as Dhamma Mahamatras?
hint: These officials were connected with the promotion of Dhamma.
summary: Ashoka appointed Dhamma Mahamatras to promote and administer aspects of his Dhamma policy.

title: 1490. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the construction of the Nagarjuni caves?
hint: He was the grandson and successor of Ashoka.
summary: Dasharatha, a grandson of Ashoka, dedicated the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas.

title: 1491. Which Mauryan ruler fought the Kalinga War?
hint: His reign is known for numerous rock and pillar edicts.
summary: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War, traditionally dated to around 261 BCE, before adopting a stronger policy of Dhamma.

title: 1492. Which ancient kingdom was conquered by Ashoka in the famous Kalinga War?
hint: It was located largely in present-day Odisha.
summary: Kalinga, located largely in present-day Odisha and adjoining areas, was conquered by Ashoka after the Kalinga War.

title: 1493. What did Ashoka promote after the Kalinga War?
hint: It emphasized moral conduct and peaceful coexistence.
summary: After the Kalinga War, Ashoka strongly promoted Dhamma, emphasizing moral conduct, tolerance and welfare.

title: 1494. Which Buddhist council is traditionally associated with the reign of Ashoka?
hint: It was traditionally held at Pataliputra.
summary: According to Buddhist tradition, the Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during Ashoka's reign.

title: 1495. Who is traditionally regarded as the chief monk associated with the Third Buddhist Council under Ashoka?
hint: He was a prominent Buddhist monk and scholar.
summary: Moggaliputta Tissa is traditionally associated with presiding over the Third Buddhist Council during Ashoka's reign.

title: 1496. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the inscription at Maski that helped identify Devanampiya Piyadasi as Ashoka?
hint: The inscription contains the ruler's personal name.
summary: The Maski inscription is important because it explicitly mentions Ashoka along with the title Devanampiya Piyadasi.

title: 1497. Which place is associated with the earliest known major Ashokan rock edict in Karnataka?
hint: It is located in the Raichur region of Karnataka.
summary: The Maski inscription is an important Ashokan inscription located in present-day Karnataka.

title: 1498. Which Mauryan ruler's inscriptions mention his visits and concern for Buddhist sites?
hint: One important inscription is found at Lumbini.
summary: Ashoka's inscriptions include records connected with Buddhist sites such as Lumbini, where he commemorated the birthplace of Buddha.

title: 1499. Which Buddhist site did Ashoka visit and mark as the birthplace of Gautama Buddha?
hint: It is located in present-day Nepal.
summary: Ashoka visited Lumbini and erected an inscription marking it as the birthplace of Gautama Buddha.

title: 1500. Which Mauryan ruler is associated with the Nigali Sagar inscription?
hint: The inscription is connected with a Buddhist stupa.
summary: Ashoka's Nigali Sagar inscription records his enlargement of the stupa associated with the previous Buddha Kanakamuni.
